about.title: Colton Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Colton sits at a crossroads of two major freeways, I-215 and I-10, plus busy local routes like Mt Vernon Avenue, and that mix shows up in the crash numbers: 452 injury collisions and 678 injured people in the most recent full year on record. Fridays between 5 and 7 p.m. see a noticeable jump in reported crashes, likely tied to commuter traffic merging with weekend travel heading toward the freeways. If you were hurt in one of these collisions, what happens in the days right after matters. Skid marks fade, vehicles get repaired or scrapped, and witnesses' memories blur. LawProactive doesn't practice law, but we can connect you with an independent attorney near Colton who handles these claims on contingency, meaning you owe nothing unless there's a recovery. Our service costs you nothing to use.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Speaking with an Insurer

items.title: California's Two-Year Clock Is Shorter Than You Think
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the crash date to file suit, but if a government entity (like a city street or Caltrans issue) contributed to the crash, that window can shrink to as little as six months. An attorney can flag this early so a claim doesn't get lost to a missed deadline.

items.title: Comparative Fault Means Partial Blame Doesn't End Your Claim
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if an insurer tries to pin some blame on you, you can still recover a share of damages reduced by your percentage of fault. Recorded statements to the other driver's insurer are often used to inflate that percentage, which is why it's worth pausing before you give one.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering Damages
items.desc: Unlike some states, California doesn't cap non-economic damages like pain, suffering, or loss of enjoyment of life in a typical car accident case. An attorney working on contingency has an incentive to value that side of your claim fully, since they're paid only if you recover.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a Colton car accident?
items.answer: In most cases California gives you two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit. That window can be much shorter, sometimes six months, if a government entity such as the city of Colton or Caltrans is involved, for example if a road defect on I-215 or Mt Vernon Avenue played a role. Because these deadlines vary, it helps to have someone review the specifics of your crash early.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: Not without talking to an attorney first. Insurance adjusters often ask questions designed to get you to downplay your injuries or accept partial blame, which can reduce what you're owed under California's comparative fault rules. An independent attorney can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: Why do so many Colton crashes seem to happen on Friday evenings?
items.answer: Public crash records show reported collisions in Colton tend to peak on Fridays between 5 and 7 p.m., which lines up with heavier traffic where I-215 and I-10 meet local streets like Mt Vernon Avenue. This is a pattern, not a judgment about any particular road. If you were injured during that window, evidence like traffic camera footage or 911 call logs can be time-sensitive, so acting quickly matters.
